newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK exporter fined for "made in Hong Kong" labels.
newsitem.headline: HK exporter fined for "made in Hong Kong" labels.

text.p: A Hong Kong court fined a garment exporter on Thursday for sticking "made in Hong Kong" labels on Chinese-made textile products before shipping them to Denmark, the government said.
The fine of HK$365,000 ($47,220) slapped on Hermes Textile Industry Ltd came as the U.S. and Hong Kong governments continued a dispute over illegal textile transshipments.
In June, Washington imposed stringent new requirements requiring Hong Kong textile exporters to provide additional import documentation on a variety of clothing products.

The aim of the extra documents was to prevent illegal transhipments passing from China through Hong Kong. Washington said goods from China were dodging U.S. quota limits with false "made in Hong Kong" labels.
